title: Audit Log Sampling Strategy & Evidence Capture Framework (SOC 2 / ISO)
content:
Executive summary:

This working playbook proposes a defensible, repeatable sampling approach and automated evidence capture framework for RBAC v2 changes, audit log exports, and SIEM-derived artifacts to support SOC 2 and ISO 27001 auditors. It focuses on three goals: (1) demonstrate that access provisioning and changes are authorized and logged, (2) provide traceable evidence for configuration and enforcement of RBAC v2, and (3) ensure SIEM exports and evidence automation meet auditor expectations for chain-of-custody, retention, and reproducibility.

Scope and context:
- Systems in-scope: control plane APIs (RBAC policy store), identity provider integrations (SCIM/OIDC), serving runtime control-plane (role bind/unbind events), and SIEM exports from our Elastic/Chronicle pipeline.
- Evidence types: raw audit-log extracts, signed export manifests, access review screenshots/export CSVs, change approval tickets, and automated rule validation reports.
- Exclusions: ephemeral debug logs that do not contain access or authorization decisions.

Why a sampling strategy?
Full-population evidence is infeasible for long retention windows and high-volume systems. Auditors accept statistically defensible samples plus targeted samples of sensitive or anomalous events. This doc defines a hybrid approach: periodic statistical sampling + risk-based targeted sampling + audit-triggered extraction.

Audit log schema (recommended canonical fields) — mapping to auditor expectations:
Provide a consistent canonical export schema that our SIEM and export pipeline translate to. Minimal required fields for auditor review:
- event_id (UUID)
- recorded_at (ISO8601 UTC)
- source_system (string: e.g., auth-service, admin-api, scim-sync)
- actor_id (internal user id or service principal)
- actor_identity (email or external idp sub)
- actor_role_at_event (role snapshot string, e.g., role:billing-admin@v2)
- action (string: e.g., role.grant, role.revoke, policy.update, login)
- resource_type (e.g., service-account, model, dataset)
- resource_id (opaque id)
- outcome (success | failure | denied)
- request_id (correlation id)
- prev_state_ref (hash or version id for prior role/policy state)
- change_delta (human-readable summary or JSON diff)
- raw_payload_ref (s3 path / GCS path)
- exported_by (automation id or username)
- export_manifest_id (for chain-of-custody)

Map to controls: short mapping examples (not exhaustive)
- SOC 2 CC6: logical access monitoring — use event.action in combination with actor_role_at_event and outcome to show enforcement and detection.
- ISO 27001 A.9: access control — exports show role assignment, modifications, and periodic reviews.
- ISO 27001 A.12.4: logging and monitoring — retention, integrity, and export manifests demonstrate completeness and integrity.

Sampling strategy (hybrid):
1) Baseline periodic sample (weekly)
   - Population: all RBAC change events for the week (role.grant, role.revoke, policy.update).
   - Sample size: for populations >5k events/week, sample 100 events chosen uniformly at random; for <5k sample 5% with minimum 30.
   - Rationale: gives longitudinal coverage and is easy to reproduce.

2) Risk-based targeted sample (daily for high-risk)
   - Risk criteria: events involving privileged roles (admin, infra, billing), cross-tenant role grants, or policy changes that widen permissions.
   - Sample rule: include 100% of high-risk events during the period.

3) Anomaly-driven sample (ad-hoc)
   - Triggered by SIEM alerts (unexpected mass grants, spike in denied outcomes, or unusual actor behavior).
   - Include all events correlated to the alert window + 24 hours before/after.

4) Auditor-requested extracts
   - On demand, provide time-bounded, signed export bundles with manifest and hash verification.

Evidence capture and automation pipeline (recommended pattern):
- Source logging: services dump canonical audit JSON to internal Kafka topic with event metadata and persistence to raw S3 (immutable).
- Processing: ETL job normalizes fields to canonical schema and writes a daily partitioned NDJSON export to s3://redwood-audit-exports/YYYY/MM/DD/
- SIEM ingestion: export consumer streams canonical events into Elastic/Chronicle and runs correlation rules.
- Export automation: a lambda/worker creates a signed export bundle (tar.gz) containing the NDJSON slice + manifest.json + SHA256 checksums and stores it to s3://redwood-audit-manifests/{manifest_id}/. The manifest contains: manifest_id, created_by, time_range, query_filter, record_count, sha256_of_bundle.
- Proof of custody: manifest_id is logged back into a ledger (immutable DynamoDB with write-once semantics + timestamp) and an entry is emitted to our audit-topic for cross-checking.

Checklist for each export bundle (auditor-facing):
- [ ] Export manifest (manifest_id, generator, UTC time range)
- [ ] SHA256 checksum of bundle and per-file checksums
- [ ] Query/filter used to generate the slice (exact query text)
- [ ] Link to raw S3 partitions and offsets used
- [ ] Mapping of canonical fields to original log fields (source_system mappings)
- [ ] Approval record or automation id that created the bundle
- [ ] Ticket or Slack thread reference when export initiated (if manual)

SIEM export mapping examples (how to present to auditors):
- SIEM field: host.timestamp -> canonical.recorded_at
- SIEM field: auth.user.email -> canonical.actor_identity
- SIEM field: event.action.keyword -> canonical.action
- SIEM field: event.outcome -> canonical.outcome
- SIEM field: ecs.version (or vendor meta) -> canonical.source_system
- In audit bundles include a small csv: field_mapping.csv with two columns: canonical_field, source_field_example.

Defensible sampling math (short):
- If an auditor asks for confidence levels, use simple binomial sampling assumptions. For example, sampling 100 events for a large population approximates a 95% confidence interval for event-level proportions with ~10% margin of error. Be ready to explain trade-offs and show targeted sampling of high-risk events for 100% coverage.

Gap analysis (current -> desired -> remediation owner / ETA):
- Gap: No exported manifest artifact for early 2024 rolling dumps.
  - Desired: All future exports have manifest + checksum.
  - Owner: Diego Alvarez (infra) — ETA: 2026-01-15 (complete).
- Gap: RBAC v2 stored role snapshots are not versioned in one canonical store (snapshots exist but split across services).
  - Desired: central role-version snapshot API and prev_state_ref in logs.
  - Owner: Rina Suresh (auth) — ETA: 2026-04-01 (in_progress).
- Gap: Evidence for periodic access reviews lacks signed reviewer confirmation (only tickets).
  - Desired: reviewers sign review using SSO and manifest included.
  - Owner: Maya Patel (secops) — ETA: 2026-03-01 (in_progress).

Auditor Q&A prep (anticipated questions + suggested answers):
Q: How do you ensure the logs are complete and not backfilled/altered after the fact?
A: Raw events are written to an immutable S3 partition with write-once lifecycle. Any downstream processing writes derived artifacts; all export manifests contain pointers to raw partitions and include a hash of the raw partition offsets. We also maintain an append-only ledger entry per manifest in DynamoDB with a server-signed timestamp.

Q: How do you demonstrate that RBAC changes were authorized?
A: Each RBAC change event contains request_id linking to the provisioning workflow (ticket or API call). For manual changes, the ticket (JIRA key) and approver identity are included in the change_delta; for automated flows, the automation id and policy id are referenced. We surface these fields in the export manifest.

Q: What is your role definition and how do you version roles?
A: Roles carry a semantic name and a version tag (e.g., billing-operator@v2). role snapshots at the time of the event are recorded in actor_role_at_event and prev_state_ref points to the prior snapshot id. Role definitions are stored in the role registry service which provides an API to retrieve historical snapshots.

Q: How do you handle third-party identity providers (SCIM)?
A: SCIM syncs emit scim.sync events that include scim_sync_job_id and mapping of external id -> internal actor_id. We include scim_sync_job_id in manifests to show the lineage.

Operational runbook (short, for evidence producers):
1) Run daily canonical export generator (00:30 UTC) -> writes partition + temp manifest.
2) Automated integrity check computes SHA256, writes final manifest to manifest-store and pushes manifest event to audit topic.
3) Weekly sampling job reads the population, selects sample, and creates an auditor bundle (sample_manifest).
4) Security owner reviews sample bundle, attaches approval note, and marks the sample run complete in the compliance tracker.

Deliverables for auditor intake (what to hand over):
- 2 weeks of weekly sample bundles (as NDJSON) + manifests.
- 100% of high-risk event bundles for the audit period.
- Role definition snapshots for any roles in sampled events.
- Access review records (signed exports) covering the audit window.
- SIEM correlation rule configs used to surface the alerts leading to anomaly samples.

Practical tips and gotchas:
- Always include the exact query text used to extract slices — auditors will re-run or ask for reproduction.
- Prefer canonical field names in exports; include mapping file to raw fields for transparency.
- Keep sample seeds documented (random seed + algorithm) so statistical sampling is reproducible.
- If a manual export occurs, capture the Slack/JIRA link and add it to the manifest as evidence of intent and authorization.

Open items & next steps:
- Rina: deliver role-version API design doc (due 2026-02-28).
- Diego: finalize export manifest schema and implement write-once manifest ledger (due 2026-01-15, complete).
- Maya: coordinate with GRC to finalize auditor intake checklist and threshold for when auditors require larger sample sizes (due 2026-03-10).

Appendix A — Example minimal manifest.json (human readable):
{
  "manifest_id": "m-20260217-0001",
  "created_by": "audit-bundle-generator-v1",
  "time_range": "2026-02-10T00:00:00Z/2026-02-16T23:59:59Z",
  "record_count": "1274",
  "query_filter": "action IN (\"role.grant\", \"role.revoke\") AND resource_type=\"service-account\",
  "bundle_sha256": "<hex>",
  "raw_partitions": "s3://redwood-audit-raw/2026/02/10/part-0001, s3://...",
  "field_mapping_file": "field_mapping.csv"
}

Appendix B — Example Splunk/KQL queries (sanitized):
- Count of privileged grants in last 90 days: index=audit action="role.grant" role IN ("admin","infra-admin") | stats count by actor_identity
- Events with outcome=denied around mass-login: index=audit outcome="denied" | where timestamp > relative_time(now(), -24h)

Contact and review cadence:
- Weekly sync with infra+secops to review export health (owners: Diego + Maya).
- Monthly evidence readiness review with GRC and product security (owners: Maya + Rina).

This doc is a working draft intended to be iterated on during the upcoming SOC 2 readiness sprint. Questions, corrections, and suggestions welcome — comment inline or ping @Maya in #compliance.
